title: Reverse String
description:
# Reverse String

Write a function that reverses a string. The input string is given as a character array `s`, and the function must modify `s` directly.

You must reverse the array **in-place** with `O(1)` extra memory. That means you may use a constant number of variables, but you should not build another array or return a new string.

## Example 1:

**Input:** s = ["h","e","l","l","o"]
**Output:** ["o","l","l","e","h"]

## Example 2:

**Input:** s = ["H","a","n","n","a","h"]
**Output:** ["h","a","n","n","a","H"]

## Constraints:

*   `1 <= s.length <= 10^5`
*   `s[i]` is a printable ASCII character.

solutions.name: Two-Pointer Temporary Swap
solutions.description:
## Approach

Place one pointer at the left end and one pointer at the right end. Swap those two characters, then move both pointers inward until they meet or cross.

## Key Insight

Reversal pairs each index `i` with index `n - 1 - i`. Swapping each symmetric pair exactly once reverses the whole array without allocating another array.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(n), because each character is touched at most once as part of a swap.
- Space Complexity: O(1), because only two indices and one temporary character are used.

solutions.name: Mirror Index For Loop
solutions.description:
## Approach

Iterate `i` through the first half of the array. For every `i`, compute its mirror index `j = n - 1 - i` and swap `s[i]` with `s[j]`.

## Key Insight

The loop length is exactly `n / 2` because each swap fixes two positions. For odd lengths, the center character maps to itself and does not need to move.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(n), because the first half of the array is scanned once.
- Space Complexity: O(1), because the algorithm stores only indices and a temporary character.

solutions.name: XOR Swap Variant
solutions.description:
## Approach

Use the same outside-in pointer movement, but exchange the two characters with three XOR operations instead of a temporary variable.

## Key Insight

XOR swap only works safely when the two indices are different, so the loop condition must be `left < right`. This is mainly a bit-manipulation teaching variant; the temporary-variable swap is usually clearer.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(n), because each symmetric pair is processed once.
- Space Complexity: O(1), because no additional array is allocated.

solutions.name: Printable ASCII Arithmetic Swap
solutions.description:
## Approach

Because the prompt restricts characters to printable ASCII, two character values can be added and subtracted without leaving the Java `char` range. Use this arithmetic identity to swap each symmetric pair.

## Key Insight

This is a constraint-specific swap technique. It still uses the same mirror-pair reversal, but it demonstrates how prompt constraints can make an otherwise risky trick safe for this input domain.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(n), because every symmetric pair is processed once.
- Space Complexity: O(1), because only two indices are stored.

solutions.name: Adjacent Pull Baseline
solutions.description:
## Approach

Repeatedly move the current first element of the active prefix to the end of that prefix by adjacent swaps. Shrink the active prefix after each pass.

## Key Insight

This is still in-place and correct, but it performs many unnecessary adjacent swaps. Comparing it with mirror-pair swapping shows why the optimal solutions exchange far-apart symmetric positions directly.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(n^2), because many adjacent swaps are performed.
- Space Complexity: O(1), because the algorithm only uses loop indices and one temporary character.

tests.description: Odd-length sample reverses around the center.
Even-length sample swaps every symmetric pair.
Two-character array performs exactly one swap.
Punctuation characters are ordinary printable ASCII.
Repeated equal characters should not confuse swap logic.
Palindrome input remains visually identical after reversal.
Longer mixed-case word checks multiple odd-length swaps.
Case is preserved while positions are reversed.
Symbol punctuation tests printable ASCII beyond letters and digits.
Duplicate values with an odd length still reverse by index.
